messages:
nightly-evals-bot: [ALERT] nightly-evals v7c (sha: b3f9a2c) — conv-commons promptset: 8.7% drop in pass@1, tokenization mismatch spike on emoji-containing prompts :warning:
anya: hmm okay can someone paste a failing example? :eyes:
sam: here's one from the report - prompt: "Write a friendly reply to: "I ❤️ this feature!"" expected: friendly reply with emoji intact, got: reply where emoji split into several tokens and answer truncated
devin: ugh that smells like tokenizer normalization/byte-splitting. Did token counts change between v7b and v7c?
mira: I ran a quick compare: v7b tokenized "I ❤️ this feature!" -> ["I","▁❤️","▁this","▁feature","!"], v7c -> ["I","▁\u2764","\uFE0F","\u200D","▁this",...]. So emoji decomposed into multiple codepoints.
lex: that would change attention windows and KV cache alignment for prefix caching — could explain truncation.
anya: where was the tokenizer change introduced? commit diff?
sam: tokenizer PR was in the same release branch to add normalization for NFC -> NFD for 'compat' reasons, commit  b3f9a2c includes `unicode_normalize(nfd=True)` in tokenizer pipeline.
devin: oh no. converting to NFD will decompose emoji sequences into multiple codepoints. We should not change normalization globally for served models.
mira: confirmed locally: running `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(tok.encode('I ❤️ this feature!').tokens)"` shows the split with v7c vocab.
anya: can we reproduce generation deterministically with a seed? need to rule out sampling artifacts.
lex: ran deterministic sampling (seed=42) against both v7b and v7c: v7b returned full reply, v7c returned truncated reply exactly where decomposed emoji increased token length and pushed past max_new_tokens.
sam: so root cause: tokenizer normalization increased token count -> hits `max_new_tokens` -> truncation. Also evaluation metric looks worse because a lot of conv prompts include emoji.
devin: possible fixes: 1) revert NFD change in tokenizer pipeline for current stable model, 2) bump max_new_tokens in eval harness (temporary), 3) add emoji composition normalization step to keep grapheme clusters intact.
mira: option 3 is ideal long-term: use Unicode grapheme cluster aware normalization (NFKC? or use `regex` with \u{...} grapheme support). But that's more work.
anya: short-term we should hotfix eval and rollback tokenizer normalization on v7c. Also need to check quantized artifacts — did quantization change anything here?
lex: quantization profile unchanged in this release, no q8 variants touched. This is purely tokenization fallout.
sam: filing a rollback PR for tokenizer change now: PR #1423. Also will backfill a note in release notes about emoji behavior.
devin: I'll run a broad diff on promptset token length distribution to enumerate how many prompts are affected. command I used: 
```
python scripts/token_length_diff.py --old-vocab v7b --new-vocab v7c --promptset conv-commons
```
result: ~12% of prompts increase token count >=1, concentrated on emoji and certain non-latin punctuation.
mira: capturing a few representative failing generations and adding to the regression dataset in the eval repo. I'll upload examples to the thread.
anya: after rollback, we should re-run nightly-evals for v7c candidate and mark canary to check impact. Assigning: sam -> rollback PR, devin -> token-length diff + dashboard update, mira -> add regression examples, lex -> update rollout policy to pin v7b for hosted until triage done.
lex: pinned production alias to v7b-canary for now. :lock:
sam: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/tokenizer/pull/1423 - revert unicode_normalize(nfd=True). Adding changelog entry.
devin: re-running eval locally after applying revert patch, will post summary within 30m.
mira: added failing examples to eval-regressions/emoji-split/*.json and flagged them in the eval dashboard with tag `emoji-split-v7c`.
anya: thanks. postmortem candidate? probably a short note in release docs should suffice if rollback goes smoothly.
lex: one action item for infra: add a linter to catch normalization changes in tokenizer PRs — maybe a CI check that compares byte->token mapping for a small unicode-heavy corpus.
sam: good idea, I'll add a CI job to run `scripts/token_length_diff.py` on a unicode-sanity set.
devin: quick mitigation note: update eval harness to use `max_new_tokens=128` -> avoids some truncations but not a real fix. I'll push a temporary branch.
mira: FYI some downstream customers exposed to that conv prompts might have observed bad replies — CS ping list?
anya: yes, I'll loop in CS with a short note: "investigating emoji splitting regression, temporary rollback in progress".
sam: (reaction) :thumbsup:
nightly-evals-bot: update: rollback PR merged to branch; next canary build 1845682300 will run smoke evals.
anya: great. let's re-evaluate after the canary finishes. thanks team! :heart:
